requirement_evidence.text: Identical complete spend key/version/payload with spend_krw=10000 twice gives one Silver row and Gold spend 10000; rerunning preserves artifact bytes.
Actual DuckDB SQL and Parquet match separately frozen hand-derived account/campaign expectations. Refund aggregation precedes order/campaign joins; shared IDs across accounts do not fan out.

Late orders/refunds remain excluded until as_of advances, then restate original order dates. Corrected cumulative spend selects latest snapshot then revision; repeated complete-window publication is idempotent.

Same-version payload conflicts, schema problems and missing mappings block/quarantine the batch, preserving previous manifest and data. Local flock excludes simultaneous writers. Injected precommit and caught post-swap fsync failures, process kill and replay are tested.

Immutable manifest records raw/SQL/artifact hashes, row counts, source coverage, as_of and metric definitions. Report shows campaign/account metrics and source watermarks; incomplete/stale/zero-spend facts keep ROAS unknown.

auditable_defaults: Local POSIX filesystem only; one writer, bounded 31-day full-window replacement per root.
32 accounts, 100000 rows/table, 32 MiB CLI input, DuckDB 1 thread and 512MB, freshness 86400 seconds are implementation defaults, not measured production SLAs.
limitations: Coverage is a source assertion, not an independent proof that an upstream feed has delivered all business events.
Development and acceptance sets share a small deterministic scenario structure; no unseen production benchmark claim.
Process/power loss after atomic pointer swap may leave either complete snapshot current. Simultaneous device/rollback failure is outside the tested filesystem fault model.
This dispatch does not implement or validate model agents, LangGraph or AWS. No learner competency or production operations claim.
